title: 09. Production & Safety: Day 19 — Production-Grade I: Wrapping Agents as Services
summary: You have spent eighteen days building agents that run in a script, print to stdout, and exit. Today we make them serve real traffic.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
You have spent eighteen days building agents that run in a script, print to stdout, and exit. Today we make them serve real traffic. We take two agents you already understand conceptually — an email triage/draft agent and a meeting prep agent — and wrap them as **HTTP services** with [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/). The agent logic stays small; the production scaffolding around it is what you need to learn.

The two production concerns we focus on are: (1) **async correctness** so an agent call does not block the event loop, and (2) **typed request/response contracts** so callers know exactly what they get back. By the end of the day you will have two runnable services you can `curl` against.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
**Calling `.run_sync()` or `chain.invoke()` inside an async endpoint.** This blocks the uvicorn worker. Every other request waits. Always use `await agent.run(...)` and `await chain.ainvoke(...)`. If you must call sync code, wrap it with `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`.

**Masking errors with a generic 500.** FastAPI returns a 500 with no body if an exception bubbles up. Catch known failure modes (upstream timeout, validation error) and raise `HTTPException` with the right status code (`502` for upstream, `422` for input, `429` for rate limit). Operators will thank you.

**Forgetting request validation.** Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` with `Field(min_length=...)` gives you free 422 responses on bad input. Always set sensible bounds — a 1 MB email body will blow your context window and your bill.

**Per-process state in multi-worker deployments.** The `hits` dict in Project 1 lives in process memory. Run two uvicorn workers and each gets half the rate budget. Use Redis or another shared store for anything that must be globally consistent.

**No request timeout.** LLM calls can hang for 30+ seconds. Configure `httpx` timeouts on the model client or wrap calls with `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=20)`. Without this, one slow model call can stall a worker.
